project.name: PHOBOSIA
project.purpose: Introduce the player to the existing Mars outpost, its modules, scientific equipment, operational systems, and interaction methods.
project.primaryImplementationPrompt: Use this JSON as the Day 1 configuration source. Inspect the actual project and validate every object name, trigger registration, coordinate, camera target, task condition, and state transition before implementation.

coordinatePolicy.coordinateSystem: Use the actual coordinate system and transforms of the loaded Three.js scene.
coordinatePolicy.axisConvention: Do not assume that supplied coordinates are world-space coordinates. Verify local versus world space and the actual scene hierarchy.
coordinatePolicy.missingValues: A null coordinate means that the coordinate was not supplied. Never interpret null as zero.
coordinatePolicy.sourceOfTruth: Prefer verified scene object transforms and existing interaction registrations over manually reconstructed coordinates.

implementationApproach: Inspect the existing repository before editing.
Use existing interaction and trigger systems wherever possible.
Use the existing event bus if available.
Use the existing camera and player controller.
Use the existing task, save, fade, and transition systems if available.
Add only the smallest reusable components necessary.
Keep configuration data separate from implementation logic.
Report unresolved references instead of silently ignoring them.

dayConfiguration.title: Outpost Orientation
dayConfiguration.startingLocationPolicy: Use the existing Habitat spawn location. Do not invent a new spawn position.
dayConfiguration.missionObjective: Become familiar with the outpost, identify the purpose of its major zones and systems, inspect the configured displays, and complete the orientation checklist.

playerExperience.introductionStyle: Short explanatory introduction with a slow horizontal camera presentation.
playerExperience.normalInteractionStyle: Use existing interactions and screen renderers after the relevant introduction.

cameraPresentationDefaults.worldHeightPolicy: Keep the camera at its verified current eye height.
cameraPresentationDefaults.pitchPolicy: Keep the existing camera pitch unchanged.
cameraPresentationDefaults.rotationStyle: Small, smooth horizontal rotation only when required to frame the target.
cameraPresentationDefaults.targetSelection: Resolve actual scene objects by verified names and use their world transforms.
cameraPresentationDefaults.targetFraming: Frame the complete configured screen group or relevant section.
cameraPresentationDefaults.missingTargetFallback: Show the configured introduction panel without camera movement and log the unresolved target.

interactionDefaults.sharedTriggerPolicy: One interaction group and one wide camera presentation for all screens assigned to the same verified trigger.
interactionDefaults.independentTriggerPolicy: Separate trigger groups receive independent introductions and task definitions.

taskProgression.taskOrderPolicy: Present the tasks in the configured zone order, while allowing the player to explore already accessible areas and complete their tasks in a different order unless the existing game architecture requires otherwise.

progressCalculation.numerator: Count of unique completed task IDs where required is true.
progressCalculation.denominator: Count of unique configured tasks where required is true.

taskCompletionValidation: Every task ID in this configuration must resolve to exactly one task definition.
Every task interactionGroupId must resolve to exactly one configured interaction group.
Every required interaction group must be reachable through a verified existing interaction or an explicitly reported unresolved reference.
A missing trigger must not automatically complete its task.
An introduction-only task must not be confused with a screen-inspection task.
Resting must not count as a substitute for any other required task.

restAndDayTransition.blockedMessage: Complete the remaining outpost orientation tasks before resting.
transitionSequence: Validate that the current mission day is 1.
Validate that all required Day 1 tasks are complete.
Validate that no day transition is already in progress.
Save Day 1 task progress and completed introduction IDs.
Advance the mission day from 1 to 2 exactly once.
Use the existing intended rest or next-day spawn policy.
Restore the correct first-person camera and controls.
Finish the transition with the existing fade-in behaviour.
restAndDayTransition.fadeImplementation: Reuse the existing fade transition system where available.
restAndDayTransition.saveImplementation: Reuse the existing save system and authoritative game state.
restAndDayTransition.nextDaySpawnPolicy: Use the existing intended next-day spawn policy. If none exists, preserve the current rest location as the default pending explicit implementation decisions; do not invent a new coordinate.

stateAndEvents.authoritativeStatePolicy: Use the existing authoritative game-state or mission-state system. Do not create a second independent source of truth.
stateAndEvents.note: These are preferred conceptual responsibilities, not guaranteed existing class names. Discover actual source-code implementations before using or creating anything.
eventPolicy: Reuse existing event names and payload conventions when suitable.
Do not register duplicate event listeners.
Do not let camera presentations modify task progress.
Do not let screen renderers advance the mission day.
Do not let repeated task events increment progress twice.
Do not emit DAY1_COMPLETED until every required task is complete.

validationAndErrorHandling.missingTargetFallback: Show the introduction panel without camera movement.
validationAndErrorHandling.missingTriggerFallback: Keep the interaction unavailable, log the unresolved reference, and report it. Never silently mark the task complete.
validationAndErrorHandling.invalidConfigurationFallback: Provide a clear development-time error and avoid starting an invalid interaction.

acceptanceTests.description: The player begins at the existing Habitat spawn.
acceptanceTests.expected: No unintended player teleport or spawn change occurs.

acceptanceTests.description: The Habitat introduction plays once at the start of Day 1.
acceptanceTests.expected: The introduction explains the Habitat and uses the configured horizontal camera presentation.

acceptanceTests.description: The player presses Enter during an introduction.
acceptanceTests.expected: The presentation stops immediately and the normal first-person view and controls are restored.

acceptanceTests.description: The camera plays a configured introduction.
acceptanceTests.expected: Camera movement is slow and horizontal, with no vertical movement, vertical tilt, roll, or abrupt motion.

acceptanceTests.description: The Habitat shared monitor trigger is activated.
acceptanceTests.expected: All three Habitat status displays are presented together as one group, provided the scene validation confirms their mapping.

acceptanceTests.description: An Engineering shared trigger is activated.
acceptanceTests.expected: One wide presentation is used for that section, not a separate presentation for every screen.
The presentation is skipped but its associated task remains incomplete until its configured completion condition is satisfied.

acceptanceTests.description: The player revisits a previously inspected section.
acceptanceTests.expected: Completed tasks remain complete and duplicate progress is not added.

acceptanceTests.description: The player interacts with the rest trigger while required tasks remain.
acceptanceTests.expected: The day does not advance and a clear message explains that tasks remain.

acceptanceTests.description: The player rests after completing every required task.
acceptanceTests.expected: The state is saved, the screen fades out and back in, and the mission advances from Day 1 to Day 2 exactly once.

acceptanceTests.description: A configured object or trigger cannot be resolved.
acceptanceTests.expected: The issue is logged and reported. No replacement object, fabricated coordinate, or automatic task completion is introduced.

acceptanceTests.description: The Day 1 implementation is built and run.
acceptanceTests.expected: The build and actual test results are reported honestly, including any tests that could not be performed.

required: Reusable introduction and horizontal camera-presentation behaviour.
Day 1 task tracking integrated with the existing state system.
Task-progress UI integrated with the existing HUD or interface.
Validated Habitat rest and Day 1-to-Day 2 transition.
Save/load integration using the existing save format where available.
finalReportMustInclude: Actual trigger mappings verified from the repository.
Unresolved screen references and missing coordinates.
Commands run and actual test results.
